reading.body:
Amazon Web Services recorded $717 billion in revenue in 2025 while operating two major AI product lines: SageMaker for full-stack ML lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model access.

AWS sits at the intersection of compute supply and AI demand. SageMaker's architecture—unified data lakes, model monitoring, bias detection, and governance tools—reflects the infrastructure required to run production AI at scale. Bedrock's API model with VPC support and IAM integration suggests AWS is positioning itself as the managed layer between foundation models and enterprise users who want isolation and control. Both products point to a company treating AI not as a feature but as a platform business spanning data, compute, and model serving.

The scale here matters for power and buildings. A $717 billion revenue company in cloud services operates data centers globally to deliver these products. The fact that SageMaker includes toxicity detection, guardrails, and data lineage tracking indicates AWS is building compliance and observability into the compute layer itself. This is not decorative. As regulatory exposure grows, the infrastructure provider that bakes governance into the platform gains advantage over those that bolt it on later.

The data does not specify AWS's capital spending, energy consumption, or data center locations. It does not break out AI revenue from total AWS revenue or show whether SageMaker and Bedrock are growing faster than legacy services. It does not name which foundation models Bedrock serves or how much compute AWS allocates to these two products versus others.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a subsidiary of Amazon, a public company founded in 1994 and headquartered in Seattle, WA, trading on public markets under the ticker AMZN. The company's most recently reported annual revenue was $716,924,000,000 for the period ending December 31, 2025. The website reviewed for this profile is the Amazon SageMaker product page, which describes SageMaker as a unified environment for data, analytics, and machine learning.

AWS offers two tracked AI products. Amazon SageMaker is described by the company as a next-generation platform bringing together ML and analytics capabilities in a single development environment called SageMaker Unified Studio. The site says it supports model development tools including HyperPod, JumpStart, and MLOps, along with generative AI application building, data processing, SQL analytics, and governance features such as fine-grained access controls, toxicity detection, and data lineage tracking. The platform integrates with Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, and AWS Glue, and incorporates Amazon Q Developer as an AI assistant for development tasks. AWS Bedrock is a separately tracked product described as a managed foundation model API service with IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and an AgentCore component for agent orchestration.

The held facts record 72 law exposure entries associated with Washington state but list no specific cases or litigation. AWS carries a CIK of 0001018724 with SEC filings on record, and its profile was verified on September 3, 2026. No MCP server registry presence is recorded.
